title: Delhi
name: Delhi
intro: Delhi is the only state in this archive whose assembly did not exist when the 1976 delimitation was made. The Legislative Assembly was abolished in 1956 under the States Reorganisation Act, and Delhi was governed for the next thirty-six years without one. It returned only with the Sixty-ninth Amendment, and the seventy constituencies on the left were drawn for that new assembly by the Election Commission in September 1992, using provisional 1991 census figures. They were contested three times, in 1993, 1998 and 2003, before the 2008 order replaced them.

map_caveats: The pre-2008 boundaries published here have been georectified. The source digitisation was displaced by roughly five kilometres and was about two and a half per cent too large relative to the post-2008 layer, which would have made any comparison between the two maps meaningless. The correction was fitted on the outer boundary of the National Capital Territory, which is fixed in law and identical under both orders, and was then tested against the constituencies that kept their names across the redraw, none of which was used to fit it: their average overlap rises from four per cent to fifty-five per cent, and the number with no overlap at all falls from thirty-four to one. The two outlines agree to an intersection-over-union of 0.95 after correction. Readers comparing these boundaries against the source digitisation should expect them to differ, by design.

Territory lineage is given for all seventy seats in both orders, on two different footings, and each seat record states which applies to it. For twenty of the seventy pre-2008 seats the link is derived from the text of the 1992 and 2008 orders, which name villages and census towns in common. For the remaining fifty the two orders share no vocabulary: the 1992 order describes seats by 1991 census charges and blocks, the 2008 order by municipal ward and enumeration block numbers, and these do not map onto one another. For those seats the successor shown is the one holding the largest share of the old seat's area, inferred from the boundaries alone and labelled as such.
Territory percentages are measured from the mapped boundaries in every case, and are areal shares, not shares of the electorate.
Elector counts are not published for Delhi. The Election Commission's statistical reports for the relevant elections were not available when this page was compiled.

Both maps are grouped by Delhi's eleven revenue districts. Neither the 1992 order nor the 2008 order assigns constituencies to districts, and the pre-2008 digitisation carried a parliamentary constituency field that was unusable, so each seat is grouped by the district its territory mostly falls within.
footnotes: Delhi's assembly seats were not delimited by the 1976 order, which covered the territory's parliamentary constituencies only. The seventy assembly constituencies were created by the Election Commission under section 38 of the Government of National Capital Territory of Delhi Act, 1991.
Reservation status (SC) reflects the category in force at the time of the relevant order, not any later reclassification.
